accessibility:
- **A name for every button:** the types require `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` on a
  `FloatButton` and a speed dial's trigger, and an empty one warns in development. Back to top's
  defaults to "Back to top". With `showLabel` or `showLabels`, the name is the text on the button,
  so what a voice control user reads is what they say
  ([WCAG 2.5.3](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/label-in-name)).
- **The tooltip doesn't repeat the name:** it shows the name to sighted users on hover and keyboard
  focus, and it's hidden from assistive technology, with no `aria-describedby` on the button, so a
  screen reader hears the name once. It stays while the pointer moves onto it, and Escape hides it,
  as every [`Tooltip`](https://bestax.io/docs/api/components/tooltip) does.
- **The speed dial is a menu button**
  ([APG](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menu-button/)): the trigger has
  `aria-haspopup="menu"` and `aria-expanded`, and `aria-controls` while the menu is open. The menu
  is named by the trigger and holds `menuitem`s. Only activation opens it, never focus, so a
  keyboard user who Tabs past it isn't shown a menu, and `openOnHover` answers the pointer alone.
  Closed actions aren't rendered, so they aren't in the accessibility tree.
- **Back to top moves focus:** after it scrolls, focus goes to the top of the content, so the next
  Tab starts there and the next Shift+Tab doesn't scroll back to the bottom
  ([WCAG 2.4.3](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-order)). Focus moves without
  scrolling, so it doesn't cut the scroll short. Hidden, the button is out of the Tab order and the
  accessibility tree.
- **Reduced motion:** back to top's scroll is instant, and its fade and the speed dial's are off,
  for someone who prefers reduced motion
  ([WCAG 2.3.3](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/animation-from-interactions)). The
  browser's smooth scroll doesn't stop on its own for that preference, so the component checks it.
- **Focus not obscured:** a float button can cover a focused link near its corner. Give `html` a
  `scroll-padding-bottom` for a bottom-corner button, as
  [Affix's accessibility notes](https://bestax.io/docs/api/components/affix#accessibility) show
  ([WCAG 2.4.11](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-not-obscured-minimum)).
- **Reading and Tab order are DOM order,** whatever corner it shows in, so write it after the
  page's main content. In a speed dial, the trigger comes first and then the actions, nearest
  first, so the reading order and the arrows agree.
- **Forced colors:** the shadow drops out, and every float button keeps an outline inside its edge
  there, colored ones too, so it stays on the page. Keyboard focus, and `isFocused`, widen it in the
  system's highlight color. The default icons draw in `currentColor`.
- **Right-to-left:** the corner and `direction` are physical, so a dial that runs left still runs
  left, and its arrows still follow the screen. The dial reads the writing direction the browser
  computes, so a `dir` attribute and a CSS `direction` both count.
summary: The `FloatButton` component renders a round icon button that floats in a corner of the screen, with its name as a tooltip. It's an `IconButton` with `isRounded`, which is a circle at every size, inside an `Affix` in its corner, and it takes what `IconButton` takes. Its name, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`, is required, and the `aria-label` shows as a tooltip on hover and keyboard focus that a screen reader doesn't read a second time. Several in one corner go in `FloatButtons`, a trigger that opens a few related actions is `FloatButton.SpeedDial`, and `FloatButton.BackToTop` scrolls back to the top of the page.

Its name, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`, is required, and the `aria-label` shows as a tooltip on hover and keyboard focus that a screen reader doesn't read a second time. props.name: as
props.description: Render as a `<button>`, an `<a>`, or a custom component such as a router `Link`, as on `IconButton`.

props.name: showLabel
props.description: Prints the `aria-label` beside the icon as the button's text, a pill (MUI's extended FAB), in place of the tooltip, for touch screens, where a tooltip never shows. It renders through `Button` then, with no `aria-label` attribute, since the text names it. A development build warns when there's no `aria-label` to print, as with `aria-labelledby`, and the button stays an icon.

props.name: color
props.description: Bulma color, as `Button`'s. Unset, it's Bulma's default button.

props.name: size
props.description: `'small'` (30px), `'normal'` (40px, the same as unset), `'medium'` (50px) or `'large'` (60px), as `Button`'s.

props.name: position
props.description: The corner it's fixed to, as `Affix`'s. Inside `FloatButtons` or a `FloatButton.SpeedDial`, which place it, it's ignored.

props.name: portal
props.description: Renders it into another container, as `Affix`'s `portal` does. Inside `FloatButtons` or a `FloatButton.SpeedDial` it's ignored.

props.name: icon
props.description: The glyph. A string is an `Icon` name, drawn from the icon library `ConfigProvider` sets. An `<Icon>` renders as given, so it can carry its own `variant` or `library`. Any other node, such as an SVG or a component from an icon package, goes inside an `Icon`, which gives it the `.icon` wrapper Bulma keeps square. It's decorative: the button's name says what it does. Give the glyph here or as `children`, not both: with both, it draws `icon` and warns in development. With neither, such as an empty string from `cond ? 'trash' : ''`, the button is an empty square, and that warns in development too.

props.name: children
props.description: The glyph as children, the way Mantine, MUI and Chakra take it: an `<Icon>` renders as given, and any other node, such as an SVG, goes inside an `Icon`, as with `icon`. Left out when `icon` is given, which warns in development. Text warns too, since `aria-label` replaces it as the name: a button with text is a `Button`.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: The id of the element whose text names the button, in place of `aria-label`.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: The button's name: what a screen reader announces and what a voice control user says to press it. Required, or `aria-labelledby` in its place, since an icon has no text to name it by. Name the action ("Delete"), not the picture ("Trash"). An empty or blank one warns in development.

props.name: isLight
props.description: Applies a lighter color variant.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Displays a loading spinner, with everything inside the button hidden behind it, in forced colors (Windows' contrast themes) too. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the spinner stops and stays drawn. Bulma alone hides only the label, so the rest needs bestax's CSS loaded.

props.name: isStatic
props.description: Makes the button non-interactive.

props.name: isOutlined
props.description: Applies outlined styling (requires color).

props.name: isInverted
props.description: Applies inverted styling (requires color).

props.name: isFocused
props.description: Applies focused styling (visual only).

props.name: isActive
props.description: Applies active styling (visual only), with no `aria-pressed`. For a button that stays pressed, use `ToggleButton`.

props.name: isHovered
props.description: Applies hovered styling (visual only).

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Applies disabled styling.

props.name: className
props.description: Custom class name.

props.name: textColor
props.description: Text color helper.

props.name: bgColor
props.description: Background color helper.

extraProps.name: type
extraProps.description: On a `<button>`, `'button'`, `'submit'` or `'reset'`, and `'button'` unless you pass one of the other two, as on `IconButton`.

extraProps.name: ref
extraProps.description: Ref forwarded to the element `as` renders, typed from `as`.

parts.summary: The `FloatButton.SpeedDial` component is a float button that opens a menu of related actions, which are FloatButtons. It's an APG menu button, on Dropdown's model. Activation opens it: Enter and Space toggle it and open it on the nearest action, the arrow that points along the dial opens it on the nearest action, and the opposite arrow on the farthest. In the menu, the arrow pointing away from the trigger moves away from it and the other moves back, Home and End go to the nearest and farthest actions, and typing a letter moves to the next action whose visible text starts with it, which an icon alone has none of, so it finds actions with `showLabels`. Escape closes it and focuses the trigger, Tab closes it and lets focus move on, and a press outside closes it. Activating an action runs its `onClick`, closes the dial and hands focus back to the trigger, unless `closeOnClick` is false. Closed, the actions aren't rendered.

props.name: icon
props.description: The trigger's icon, as IconButton's `icon`: an Icon name or a node. Decorative, since the name says what it does. To swap it while the dial is open, pass a different one from a controlled `open`.

props.name: color
props.description: The trigger's Bulma color, as `Button`'s.

props.name: size
props.description: The trigger's size; the actions take their own.

props.name: children
props.description: `FloatButton`s, the actions, nearest the trigger first.

props.name: open
props.description: Whether the actions are shown. Controlled; pair it with `onOpenChange`.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether the actions are shown at first, uncontrolled.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called with the new state when it opens or closes.

props.name: openOnHover
props.description: Also opens when the pointer rests on it, after a short delay, through the hook under HoverCard and Tooltip, and closes once the pointer and focus have left the trigger and the actions. The pointer only: keyboard focus on the trigger never opens it, and a touch pointer doesn't either. Activation still toggles it, which is how the keyboard opens it, so a click on a dial the pointer opened closes it. It isn't Dropdown's `hoverable`, which opens on hover in place of a click, through CSS alone: this opens on hover as well as a click, and the open state, `aria-expanded` and `onOpenChange` follow it.

props.name: closeOnClick
props.description: Closes the dial when an action is clicked, or activated with Enter or Space, and hands focus back to the trigger, as Dropdown's does. Off, the dial stays open and focus stays on the action.

props.name: direction
props.description: The way the actions run from the trigger, on the screen, in right-to-left text too. The arrow key that points that way moves away from the trigger. Unset, it's `'up'` from a bottom corner and `'down'` from a top one.

props.name: showLabels
props.description: Prints every action's `aria-label` beside it, as each one's `showLabel` does, for touch screens, where a tooltip never shows. Unset inside `FloatButtons`, it's the stack's `showLabels`.

props.name: position
props.description: The corner, as `Affix`'s. Inside `FloatButtons`, which places it, it's ignored.

props.name: portal
props.description: As `Affix`'s `portal`. Inside `FloatButtons` it's ignored.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: The id of the element whose text names the button, in place of `aria-label`.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: The button's name: what a screen reader announces and what a voice control user says to press it. Required, or `aria-labelledby` in its place, since an icon has no text to name it by. Name the action ("Delete"), not the picture ("Trash"). An empty or blank one warns in development.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional CSS classes.

parts.summary: The `FloatButton.BackToTop` component is a float button that shows once the page has scrolled down, and takes it back to the top. It renders nothing on the server, and after hydration a scroll listener shows it past `visibilityHeight` and hides it above. Hidden, it keeps its place in a `FloatButtons` stack, out of the Tab order and the accessibility tree. Activated, it scrolls the page, or `scrollContainer`, to the top, smoothly or at once when the user prefers reduced motion, and moves focus to the top of the content (`moveFocus`), so the next Tab starts there rather than back where the page was.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: The button's name, and its tooltip's text. Pass your own to translate it. An empty one keeps the default rather than leaving the button unnamed.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: The id of an element whose text names it, in place of `aria-label`. No tooltip then.

props.name: icon
props.description: The icon. Unset, an up arrow drawn in `currentColor`, as Carousel's arrows are.

props.name: visibilityHeight
props.description: How far the page, or `scrollContainer`, has to scroll before the button shows, in pixels.

props.name: scrollContainer
props.description: The element that scrolls, when it isn't the window: an element, a ref, or a `document.querySelector` selector. The button watches it and scrolls it. It's found when the button mounts and when this prop changes, so a ref whose element changes later isn't followed, and one that finds nothing leaves the button on the window.

props.name: moveFocus
props.description: Where focus goes after it scrolls, shaped like `useFocusTrap`'s `restoreFocus`. `true` focuses the page's `<main>`, or the `scrollContainer` when there is one, or else `<body>`; a ref focuses that element; `false` moves none, so the button hides with focus on it once the scroll is done, focus drops to the document, and the next Tab starts wherever the browser decides. Focus moves with `preventScroll`, at once, so it doesn't cut the scroll short. An element that can't take focus gets `tabindex="-1"`, and no focus ring, until it loses it, so the next Tab goes on from there. A tabindex of its own is left alone.

props.name: showLabel
props.description: Prints the `aria-label` beside the icon as the button's text, a pill (MUI's extended FAB), in place of the tooltip, for touch screens, where a tooltip never shows. It renders through `Button` then, with no `aria-label` attribute, since the text names it. A development build warns when there's no `aria-label` to print, as with `aria-labelledby`, and the button stays an icon.
